name: Alex Miranda
life: “I still remember keeping my dad's car seat free of greasy tools.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Alex by a small Thursday habit. Alex checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I own the van and want a clean seat for my father on the way home from his appointment.
appearance: Alex is easy to recognize by a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears and heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining, Alex touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word when listening.
personality: Alex is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Alex is concerned.
agenda: To keep one clean seat for the father.
family: Paloma Diaz is Alex’s stepsibling. Alex chooses the music. Paloma puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Saturday keys*, Paloma says, “I had the locks changed before they found the keys.”
connections: Lou Carver. A reserved passenger seat and a Friday prescription become two explicit parts of the carpool.
